title: The Present Indicative Passive
subtitle: amor, amāris, amātur. The -r endings.
objectives: Conjugate any verb in the present passive across all conjugations.
Translate passive sentences with and without expressed agent.
Understand that the agent of a passive verb is expressed with ā/ab + ablative.
Recognize that passive forms use -r instead of active -ō, -m, -t.

sections.heading: The passive voice
sections.body:
The passive voice shows that the subject is acted upon. amō means 'I love'; amor means 'I am loved'.

Present passive endings:
  -or, -ris, -tur, -mur, -minī, -ntur

First conjugation passive:
  amor, amāris, amātur, amāmur, amāminī, amantur

The agent (by whom) is expressed with ā or ab + ablative:
  amor ā puellā. — I am loved by the girl.

Cicero writes: Catilīna ā cōnsule accūsātur. — Catiline is accused by the consul.
Caesar writes: oppidum oppugnātur. — The town is being attacked.

items.prompt: Conjugate videō in the present passive.
items.answer: videor, vidēris, vidētur, vidēmur, vidēminī, videntur
The girl is praised by the master.
